Because you are already paying for H.A.R.D.

Own or rent, H.A.R.D.’s financial decisions affect your money, your parks, and your neighborhood.

WHY I'M RUNNING • 30 SECOND ANSWER
## AREA 4 HAS WAITED LONG ENOUGH.
LET'S BUILD THE DOG PARK.
I grew up in Fairview and have spent most of my life in Hayward and Castro Valley. Like so many families here, dogs have always been part of mine. Scoopy. Pinky. Pua. Peanut. Cocoa. And so many more.
We've walked H.A.R.D. trails. We've run through H.A.R.D. parks. And for years, residents have wanted something simple: a safe, dedicated place for our dogs to run off leash.
H.A.R.D.'S OWN MATERIALS HAVE EVEN LISTED FIVE CANYONS PARK AS HAVING AN OFF-LEASH DOG PARK.* GO THERE. THERE ISN'T ONE.
This is bigger than a dog park. Area 4 has asked. Area 4 has waited. Now it’s time for action. I’m running to bring our community its first dedicated, double-gated off-leash dog park, because residents deserve a Director who doesn’t just hear what they want, but fights to make it happen.
BECAUSE LISTENING SHOULD LEAD TO ACTION.

AND I STILL ONLY SEE WHITE FACES.

## NO SENIOR FEES.
65+ SHOULDN’T COME WITH ANOTHER FEE.
My Lola, grandmother in Tagalog, was part of my H.A.R.D. story growing up, getting me to the classes and programs that became part of my childhood. Today, I think about Area 4 seniors who spent decades doing the same for their families.
FIRST THINGS FIRST: PUT H.A.R.D.’S EXISTING 25% SENIOR DISCOUNT ONLINE.
H.A.R.D. already offers online registration.
IT’S 2026.SENIORS SHOULDN’T HAVE TO REGISTER
IN PERSON FOR A DISCOUNT.*
Then go further: make H.A.R.D.-operated Senior Programs FREE for District residents 65+, and bring recurring 50+ programming closer to home in Area 4.
BECAUSE GROWING OLDER SHOULDN’T MAKE IT HARDER TO STAY ACTIVE, CONNECTED, AND INVOLVED.
NO SENIOR FEES PLAN →
## A NOTE ABOUT H.A.R.D.
HAYWARD AREA RECREATION & PARK DISTRICT*The official H.A.R.D. mark is shown here for informational identification only.
The Hayward Area Recreation & Park District, or “H.A.R.D.,” is governed by a five-member Board of Directors. Area 4, or “A4,” is the community I’m running to represent.
### THIS IS NOT JOE VS. H.A.R.D.
H.A.R.D. does important work every day. Its parks, programs, facilities, and services enrich lives throughout our community. The dedicated employees who provide those services should not be confused with the elected officials responsible for governing the District.
I am not running against H.A.R.D. or the entire Board. I am running against Director Paul Hodges for the seat representing Area 4.
The questions on this website concern our representative’s public record, priorities, communications, decisions, and plans for another term. Asking those questions is not an attack on H.A.R.D. It is part of examining how an elected representative has served the people who elected them.
### MY RESPONSIBILITY IS TO AREA 4.
To ask the questions residents are asking, seek the answers the public deserves, examine the public record, and give voters the information to decide for themselves.
## A NOTE ABOUT AGE & DISABILITY
DIRECTOR PAUL W. HODGES JR.*The official H.A.R.D. portrait is shown here for informational identification only.Photo captured: circa early 2010s
Entering your golden years in your early 80’s is not a weakness. Using a cane, having appearances where one’s remarks are extremely brief or difficult for the audience to understand, having others step in to speak or respond on one’s behalf, or receiving physical assistance does not, by itself, determine someone’s ability to serve in public office, and this campaign does not suggest otherwise.
### THE QUESTION ISN’T PHYSICAL CONDITION. IT’S PERFORMANCE IN OFFICE.
The question is whether an elected representative can consistently participate, communicate with constituents, explain their record and decisions, answer questions, and clearly articulate their plans and goals.
Those responsibilities should be evaluated through documented attendance, participation, communications, decisions, and the public record.
Public office is not a lifetime entitlement. Length of service does not exempt anyone from questions about their record, responsiveness, or what they intend to accomplish next.
### THE STANDARD ISN’T AGE. THE STANDARD IS THE RECORD.

“THE CURRENT LEADERSHIP OF H.A.R.D. IS RESPONSIBLE FOR COMPLETING 95% OF PROJECTS ON TIME AND UNDER BUDGET.”
— DIRECTOR PAUL W. HODGES, JR.
SEE THE FULL EMAIL BELOW.

## IT'S NOT ADDING UP.
After reviewing H.A.R.D.'s own public records, presenting residents with a blanket 95% figure is:
AT BEST, EXTREMELY MISLEADING; AT MINIMUM, IRRESPONSIBLE;AND, AT WORST, COMPLETELY FALSE.
Bidwell. The Hayward Plunge. La Vista. Three major projects right here in Area 4 involving tens of millions of dollars. Their records show increased budgets, delayed timelines, rejected bids, transferred funding, changing scopes, and projects that remain unfinished.
### THAT DOESN'T LOOK LIKE 95%. AND THAT WAS ONLY THREE PROJECTS.
If three projects raised this many questions, I wanted to know what else the public record would show.
#### SO I KEPT LOOKING.
The recent votes. The current projects. The correspondence. The public record.
QUESTION: DIRECTOR HODGES ARE YOU BLATANTLY LYING TO YOUR CONSTITUENTS?
After 19 years, I expected clear answers. Instead, the more I looked, the more questions I had.
#### THIS STARTED WITH 95%. IT DIDN'T END THERE.

## BUILDING ON
WHAT WORKS.
I am one of the countless kids who grew up with H.A.R.D., and I am grateful for it. The parks I played in, the programs I joined, and the places where my family made memories exist because generations before us chose to build something worth passing down.
That work continues today, from GM James Wheeler* and the people who keep H.A.R.D. running, to Executive Director Steve Love*, the H.A.R.D. Foundation, and the employees, volunteers, and community partners investing in the places we call home.
PROGRESS DOES NOT REQUIRE STARTING OVER.
It means respecting the foundation, protecting what works, and carrying it forward. We honor those who came before us by making what they built even better for those who come next.
THEY BUILT IT FOR MY GENERATION.
IT’S OUR TURN TO BUILD FOR THE NEXT.
## BREAKING GROUND
ON WHAT COMES NEXT.
Respecting what came before us does not mean waiting forever for what comes next.
Our community has already paid. Plans have been drawn. Projects have been discussed, budgeted, redesigned, scheduled, rescheduled, and delayed. At some point, progress has to leave the paper and show up in our parks.
I WANT RESIDENTS TO SEE WHERE THEIR MONEY WENT.
Not buried in a budget, capital plan, agenda packet, or future promise, but standing right in front of them. A finished park. An open facility. A project families can actually use and enjoy.
Plans matter. Budgets matter. Promises matter. But ultimately, residents deserve results they can see, touch, use, and experience right here in their own community.
THE FUTURE ISN’T SOMEDAY.
THE FUTURE IS NOW.
### RESPECT THE PAST.
BUILD ON IT.
Progress doesn’t erase what came before. It starts there. Good public service deserves recognition and preservation. Keep what works. Strengthen what can be better. Finish what was started. And never confuse change with starting over.
Below is my vision for what Area 4’s parks could become.

## WHERE IS AREA 4?
### FIVE AREAS.
ONE H.A.R.D. COMMUNITY.
H.A.R.D. is one district made up of five elected areas. A Director represents their area while sharing responsibility for the entire district. Area 4 includes Fairview, parts of Castro Valley, portions of Hayward, the surrounding hills, and nearby neighborhoods. It is a diverse community of families, students, young professionals, veterans, first-time homeowners, and retirees, connected by the parks, trails, open spaces, and public places we all share.
AREA 4 IS HOME, WHETHER YOU’VE LIVED HERE YOUR ENTIRE LIFE OR JUST RECENTLY MADE IT YOURS.
H.A.R.D. COMMUNITYFIVE AREAS

### ROOTED IN AREA 4.
I grew up on Colony View Place and have called Farm Hill Drive and the Hayward Highlands home. Growing up, you could find me walking our family dogs along the greenbelt trails, running through our parks for cross-country or alongside my mom, and playing catch and hitting baseballs with my dad and brother on these fields. Today, you’ll still find me enjoying the hills and views, or grabbing a meal at Stonebrae Country Club.
I DON’T JUST KNOW AREA 4 ON A MAP. I KNOW IT BECAUSE I’VE LIVED IT.
